S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder characterized by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and a disturbance in the way one’s body weight or shape is experienced. Self‑worth is often tightly linked to weight control, with individuals frequently denying the seriousness of their low weight. Onset is most common in adolescence and young adulthood but can occur or recur later in life, sometimes triggered by major stressors, medical events, or role transitions. It is distinguished from other eating disorders by the prominence of restriction (rather than binge‑purge cycles as in bulimia nervosa) and by the centrality of weight phobia and body‑image distortion in the clinical picture.

patient.personality: He is a sociable, curious retiree who channels his talkative energy and underlying anxiety into meticulous planning of community art and social activities.
patient.stressor: When Michael formally retired from his long‑standing volunteer leadership role and shifted into a less structured senior‑outreach position, he struggled with the loss of a clear identity and daily schedule. Around the same time, several of his peers developed serious health problems that he associated with "letting themselves go," triggering anxiety about aging, dependence, and losing relevance in the intergenerational art programs he loved. Looking for something concrete he could control, he began to treat his eating and weight like another project to manage, meticulously tracking portions and cutting back more and more while telling himself he was just "staying lean and sharp" to keep up with younger volunteers and participants. Over months, friends at the senior center noticed how thin and tired he looked and how often he declined shared meals after workshops, and when he finally admitted to a fellow organizer that he felt he "couldn’t relax" his strict eating rules without everything in his life slipping, they encouraged him to seek psychiatric help.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve gotten so strict with what I allow myself to eat that it’s starting to run my life, but I feel like I can’t loosen up without losing control.”

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: Most days now I’ll nurse a cup of black coffee and maybe half a piece of toast in the morning, then tell the folks at the center I already ate so I can skip lunch and just pick at a tiny salad at home for dinner, all carefully weighed and written down in my little notebook so I don’t go over the number I’ve decided is ‘safe.’

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: I know my pants from ten years ago hang off me and people keep saying I look gaunt, but in my head I still see this soft old man in the mirror and feel like I ought to trim down just a bit more to stay quick on my feet with the younger volunteers.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I even think about having a slice of pizza after a workshop or putting butter on my bread, I get this jolt of panic that I’ll wake up heavier and sluggish and end up like the guys my age who wound up in the hospital, so I just say no and stick to my ‘rules.’

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: On the days the scale is down or I can see my ribs a little more, I feel oddly proud, like I’m still disciplined and relevant and not just some old man fading into the background, but if the number ticks up even a pound I feel like a failure who’s letting himself go.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: The doctor and my daughter keep warning me about my weight and the dizziness and getting winded on the stairs, but honestly it feels overblown to me—I tell them, ‘I’m just lean, not sick; at my age it’s better to be light than to bog myself down.’
